--- name: nextjs-legacy-css-cleanup description: | Systematically migrate a Next.js + React codebase from legacy CSS class-based styling to inline styles, remove orphaned global rules, and verify the build. Covers batch waves (shell → wrappers → clients → CSS) and safe deletion of unused stylesheets. category: software-development --- # Next.js Legacy CSS Cleanup ## When to use - The codebase has legacy `.qaf-*` or similarly namespaced CSS classes. - You are doing a multi-wave migration: component wrappers → page clients → global CSS. - `globals.css` has grown large with orphaned rules. - You want to delete a `.css` file and need to verify zero consumers. ## Workflow ### 1. Inline component styles first Patch each component/page that uses the legacy classes: ```tsx // Before
...
// After
...
``` Search for remaining usages: ```bash grep -rn 'className="qaf-' src/ ``` ### 2. Clean up global CSS List orphaned selectors still declared in `globals.css`: ```bash grep -on '\.qaf-[^ {]*' src/app/globals.css | sort -u ``` Because the file may be heavily compressed (single-line blocks), prefer reading line ranges with `sed -n` before patching, or use regex-based cleanup scripts for bulk removal. ### 3. Delete unused stylesheets **CRITICAL: Verify ALL consumers, not just the file you edited.** ```bash grep -rn 'dashboard.css' src/ ``` Only delete after `grep` returns zero matches and you have read the actual output. ### 4. Verify ```bash npx tsc --noEmit npx next build ``` If the dev server was running during the build, restart it afterward: ```bash pkill -f "next dev -p 4000" && rm -rf .next && npx next dev -p 4000 ``` ## Pitfalls 1. **Shared CSS files** — A stylesheet like `dashboard.css` may be imported by both `/admin/layout.tsx` AND `/dashboard/layout.tsx`. Removing one import does not make the file safe to delete. 2. **Compressed CSS** — `globals.css` may contain entire rule blocks on a single line. Standard multi-line `patch` fails; use very long unique context strings or scripted regex replacement. 3. **RTL variants** — Remember to remove `[dir="rtl"] .qaf-...` rules alongside their LTR counterparts. 4. **Intentional CSS retention** — Marketing/landing pages may deliberately keep CSS classes for design consistency. Exclude them from grep/patch scope. 5. **Accidental deletion** — If you delete a file that still has consumers, recover it immediately with: ```bash git show HEAD:src/app/dashboard.css > src/app/dashboard.css ``` ## Scripts - `scripts/cleanup-globals-css.py` — Regex-based removal of orphaned selectors from a compressed globals.css.

# Reference: Q.af CSS-cleanup session (June 2026)

## Context
Q.af uses a legacy `.qaf-*` class namespace that was migrated to inline styles in waves.
The final wave involved: component wrappers → page clients → `SidebarLayout.tsx` → `globals.css`.

## Files touched in this wave
- `src/app/admin/queues/page.tsx`
- `src/app/admin/tenants/AdminTenantsClient.tsx`
- `src/app/admin/users/AdminUsersClient.tsx`
- `src/app/admin/rules/AdminRulesClient.tsx`
- `src/components/SidebarLayout.tsx` (full rewrite to inline styles)
- `src/app/admin/layout.tsx` (removed `dashboard.css` import)
- `src/app/globals.css` (removed orphaned selectors)

## Recovery of accidentally-deleted stylesheet
`dashboard.css` was still required by `src/app/dashboard/layout.tsx` even after admin removed its import. Recovery:
```bash
git show HEAD:src/app/dashboard.css > src/app/dashboard.css
```

## Globals.css surgical removal technique
The file was heavily compressed (single-line rule blocks), so standard multi-line `patch` often failed. Preferred approach:

1. Read exact line range with `sed -n`.
2. Use a very long unique context string for `patch` (20–30 surrounding chars).
3. For bulk removal, use a Python regex script (see `scripts/cleanup-globals-css.py`).

## Orphaned selectors removed
- `.qaf-shell`, `.qaf-sidebar`, `.qaf-main`, `.qaf-topbar`
- `.qaf-card`, `.qaf-input`, `.qaf-textarea`, `.qaf-select`
- `.qaf-nav-link` (with `.active` and `:hover`)
- `.qaf-drawer`, `.qaf-drawer-scrim`, `[dir="rtl"] .qaf-drawer`
- `.drawer-head`
- `.brand-mark` (with `::after`)
- `.nav-section`
- `.dash-btn` (with `.primary`, `.ghost`, `.soft`, `.danger`, `.sm`, `.lg`, `.icon`)
- `.skeleton` and `@keyframes dash-pulse`

## Verification result
`tsc --noEmit` passed cleanly. `next build` failed only because `dashboard.css` had been deleted while still imported by `dashboard/layout.tsx`; after recovery, build was expected to pass.
